claims.statement: The proposed annotation language and tools (prob-check-py and prob-check-r) allow library developers to express statistical assumptions and automatically check them by generating hypothesis tests.
claims.evidence_quote: we introduce a simple annotation language to allow popular statistical assumption to be expressed and have an automated check generated

claims.statement: Unconfirmed statistical assumptions are widespread in popular Kaggle notebooks: 84.38% of surveyed notebooks and 53.36% of calls to annotated functions had statistically significant evidence against at least one assumption.
claims.evidence_quote: statistically significant evidence against assumptions in 84.38% of surveyed notebooks, and in 53.36% of calls to annotated functions

claims.statement: In 11.51% of hypothesis-test calls (16.47% of call sites) with unconfirmed assumptions, using a more appropriate test would have changed the conclusion.
claims.evidence_quote: at 16.47% of call sites (11.51% of calls) where an assumption was unconfirmed, the more appropriate test would have resulted in a diferent conclusion being drawn

claims.statement: The annotation burden for library developers is low: 12 annotations were needed in Python and 14 in R for common hypothesis testing and linear regression functions.
claims.evidence_quote: in total we introduced 12 annotations in Python, and 14 in R

claims.statement: Analysts rarely check assumptions manually: only 11 of 128 Kaggle notebooks check or mention all assumptions related to the statistical methods they use.
claims.evidence_quote: only 11 check or mention all of the assumptions related to the statistical methods they use

claims.statement: The automated checks identify many potential misuses: 267 call sites and 586 calls had at least one unconfirmed assumption.
claims.evidence_quote: In total, 267 call sites and 586 calls had at least one unconfirmed assumption, and so are classified as potential misuses

overall_conclusion: The paper introduces an annotation language and tools, prob-check-py and prob-check-r, that automatically check statistical assumptions by generating hypothesis tests. An evaluation on 128 Kaggle notebooks found unconfirmed assumptions in 84.38% of notebooks and 53.36% of calls, and 11.51% of hypothesis-test calls would have reached different conclusions with more appropriate tests. The annotation burden was low: 12 annotations in Python and 14 in R.
comparable_notes: Fair comparison should consider the corpus selection protocol: 128 Kaggle notebooks were chosen by references to annotated functions, manually validated for actual calls, public data, runtime <=10 minutes, and error-free execution, targeting 15 notebooks per function. Assumptions were encoded from documentation and statistical literature. Checks used a significance level of 0.95 in annotations, except some regression residual checks at 0.05. Significant misuse was determined by comparing p-values from original and appropriate non-parametric/alternative tests against analyst-chosen significance levels, commonly 0.05 or 0.01; independence-related cases were not re-tested because they require domain knowledge.
